intro: One locus, three carriers it might run on. Its seal is printed above it.

steps.caption: L runs on a thread. Its identity is its seal — the hash of its canonical form — not the thread.
The thread is replaced. L moves to a core. The seal did not change, because nothing about L was ever defined in terms of the thread.
steps.takeaway: No property of a locus is defined in terms of the thread, core or process currently carrying it.

steps.caption: The core is replaced by a machine. Same seal.
steps.takeaway: A Carrier is a replaceable execution embodiment — a standing rule in ComputeDriven since R2.1.

steps.caption: The machine goes away. L has no carrier. Is L gone? Dormant But Alive is the pattern that answers.
steps.takeaway: Carrier Identity is the anti-pattern: 'the thing is the thread running it'. It is how a restart becomes a death.
